chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from the one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding Barirah: there are three Sunnahs when she was emancipated: regarding the choice, and regarding the charity, and regarding the mastership.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرِ: The choice, specifically the right of a slave woman to choose to remain with her husband upon emancipation.
key_terms.السُّنَنِ: Sunnahs, here referring to established legal practices or precedents.
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: The charity, referring to the payment made to free her.
key_terms.الْوَلَاءِ: Mastership, the legal bond of ownership that transfers upon emancipation.
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a slave girl whose emancipation case established several legal precedents.

ai.seo_question: What are the three Sunnahs regarding the emancipation of Barirah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam Ali’s (AS) establishment of three foundational legal principles regarding Barirah: the right of choice (khayr) in marriage, the attribution of manumission charity (sadaqah) to the payer, and the retention of original mastership (walayah). These rulings, derived from the Prophet’s precedent, are central to Shia jurisprudence on manumission, emphasizing the agency of the freed slave and the economic incentives for freeing slaves. The narration underscores the continuity between the Prophet’s practice and Imam Ali’s authoritative interpretation of these social and legal norms.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding Bureyra, there are three Sunnahs when she was emancipated – regarding the choice, and regarding the charity, and regarding the mastership’.
